payload.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

ambiguities: The phrase polynomial in q could mean equality in a polynomial ring or simplification of a rational expression to a polynomial; the statement appears to intend the latter.
The coefficient ring is not stated explicitly, but the intended meaning is usually coefficients in the integers.
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is used in its standard meaning.
The phrase polynomial in q means the quotient is viewed as a polynomial in the indeterminate q.
The coefficients are taken with respect to the standard monomial basis in q.
The conclusion concerns the quotient polynomial itself, not the individual q-binomial factors.
The stated inequalities force n to be nonnegative.

domain_restrictions: n, k, and l are integers.
The bounds 0 <= k and 0 <= l and k <= n and l <= n are assumed.
The symbol [n choose k]_q refers to the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient.
The quotient is assumed to simplify to an actual polynomial in q, not merely a rational function.
Coefficients are interpreted in the usual expansion in powers of q.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n and integers k and l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the quotient of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient for n choose k by the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient for n choose l is a polynomial in q, then all coefficients of that polynomial are nonnegative.
quantifier_order: For every integer triple n, k, l.
